critical_code_review_comments: MyTeam.jsx had two parallel issues from a botched refactor: (a) orphan trailing JSX at lines 216-224 that started with `v className=` (missing `<div`) - clearly a leftover Modal closing block from a function whose top was deleted; (b) StatusPill function defined twice back-to-back. Both indicate the file was edited via partial copy/paste without re-running. Recommend running ESLint pre-commit / CI compilation gate to catch this before deployment.

server.py is now 1152 lines - severely past the 700-line threshold flagged in iter3. Approval logic, list_teams/list_players auth-aware filtering, and discipline stats keep growing in this monolith. Strongly recommend splitting into routers/services (auth, teams, players, matches, fixtures, stats, inventory, bookings, uploads).

list_teams/list_players manually decode JWT inside the list endpoint to detect admin role (lines 466-473, 532-543). This duplicates get_current_user logic and silently swallows all exceptions. Refactor by using an Optional dependency that returns user or None - cleaner and centralized.

/api/teams/{team_id}/status and /api/players/{player_id}/status take `status` as a query parameter rather than a JSON body. Works but unconventional for PUT - consider a small Pydantic body model {status: Literal['pendiente','aprobado','rechazado']} for self-documenting OpenAPI.

When admin updates a team via PUT /api/teams/{team_id}, the model_dump replaces the entire document (including status). Because TeamIn has no status field, the existing status value is wiped on every update (Pydantic dump returns nothing for it - actually Mongo $set only sets the dumped fields, so status remains). Confirmed safe but worth covering with a regression test.
PlayerIn similarly does not include status; update_player relies on $set not including status, so existing approval status persists - good. Add explicit test for this invariant.

/api/stats/discipline does not filter by tournament_id. With multiple tournaments in the DB, cards from old tournaments will count toward the current standings. Acceptable for MVP but document or add a filter.

MatchResultIn.cards is List[dict] - no schema validation on card structure. A bad payload (missing player_id or invalid type) will silently accumulate into discipline stats with `if not pid: continue`. Add a CardIn(BaseModel) {player_id, team_id, type: Literal['yellow','red'], minute: int}.

rca of the issue: RCA: The /admin/aprobaciones page and ALL pages of the SPA were inaccessible because MyTeam.jsx had a syntax error: lines 216-224 contained orphaned closing JSX from a previous Modal component (missing `<div`, starting with `v className=...`) followed by lines 217-225 which were a verbatim duplicate of the StatusPill function defined at 207-215. Webpack/babel raised SyntaxError 'Identifier StatusPill has already been declared (217:9)' (after my first partial fix) and 'Missing semicolon (216:1)' (initial state). This is a CRA dev overlay that hijacks the entire DOM, so even routes that don't import MyTeam.jsx (like /login, /admin/aprobaciones) showed only the red error overlay. Reproduction: visit any route -> overlay 'Compiled with problems'. Mitigation applied: deleted lines 216-235 (orphan + duplicate), saved file at 215 lines. After hot-reload, all pages compile and AdminApprovals fully renders. Root cause likely a botched search-replace by the main agent during iter4 implementation.
